name: NY-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+10) with incumbent Nicole Malliotakis seeking reelection
Overwhelming fundraising edge: Malliotakis has $2.77 million on hand versus $35,000 for Democrat Michael DeCillis
Prediction markets price Malliotakis around 95% to win
No public general-election polling, leaving the forecast dependent on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Malliotakis: a Republican-leaning Staten Island seat, a two-term incumbent with a massive cash advantage, and no meaningful outside spending against her. Markets agree, pricing her near 95%, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin with only a modest adjustment for her strong financial position.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing DeCillis within single digits would signal the race is more competitive than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a third term in this Staten Island-based district, which leans Republican by about ten points. Her challenger, Democrat Michael DeCillis, has raised under $70,000 and had roughly $35,000 on hand, while Malliotakis has raised $2.75 million and holds $2.77 million in cash. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

There is no public general-election polling, and no major expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give Malliotakis about a 95 percent chance of winning. The expected margin is roughly fifteen points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling. A shift in the national environment or unexpected spending could narrow the race, but the structural advantages favor the incumbent.
